paragraphs.text: Fox is a creature type used for cards depicting carnivorous mammals, characteristically having upright ears, a pointed snout, and a long bushy tail. Foxes are related to dogs and wolves .
Sapient fox folk can be found on a few planes, where they may be known as fox-folk or kitsune .

Foxes appear most often in white , though blue and green are the most common secondary colors. Zirda, the Dawnwalker and Bright-Palm, Soul Awakener are the only red -aligned foxes, while Etched Familiar is the only black -aligned one.
Arctic Foxes from Ice Age was the first Fox card, but used the pluralized form. It was the only Fox card for nearly a decade.
This changed when the Kamigawa block introduced the kitsune. In the original block, kitsune were portrayed not with conventional fox heads, but rather with kabuki kitsune masks.
After Innistrad added Silverchase Fox and Theros Vulpine Goliath , the creature type became more common but usually represented fox animals rather than fox-folk.
The kitsune returned in Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty , with an updated design. While they still retained kabuki-mask elements, their heads are more conventionally fox-like.
The first token Fox was introduced in Modern Horizons 3 on Genku, Future Shaper .

Foxs or Foxfolk are one of the animalfolk of Bloomburrow . Weaselfolk are less common than some of the animalfolk in the Valley . The most well-known foxfolk is the charming adventurer, Mr. Foxglove .
Foxes were one of the animals to survive during the Ice Age ( Arctic Foxes ).

Giant foxes are used as mounts by Elves on the plane of Eldraine ( Maraleaf Rider , Wildborn Preserver , Wildwood Tracker ). Some foxes can fly ( Flutterfox ). The elves of Redtooth Keep are cursed to become werefoxes at night .
Foxes inspired some of the works made by lifecrafters ( Filigree Familiar ), though no native foxes have appeared.

The Kitsune (KIT-soo-nay; Japanese: 狐 ; Kamigawan: kitsune-bito, lit. "foxfolk" ; 59 cards ) of Kamigawa are cunning, tricksy masters of diplomacy and swordsmanship. They are curious and fond of playing pranks, mostly harmless ones for their amusement. They tend to live in large, close-knit family clans related through blood and marriage. Kitsune are proud of their lineages and can trace their ancestry back through multiple generations.

The kitsune are long-lived beings with very strong beliefs in their traditions. The more a kitsune experiences, the more tails they grow, with the wisest elders having nine tails. The average kitsune is slightly shorter than a human, with the top of their head coming up to a person's chin. They have white fur with red markings.

Even though the kitsune live within the Jukai Forest , they have the closest relations with the humans. , even more so than the daimyo's Soratami advisors. They are most commonly found in the Imperial court .
Ikoria features elemental foxes ( Zirda, the Dawnwaker ).
On expeditions through Ashmouth , the hunters of Devilthorn Lodge rely on the cleverness of foxes to counteract the mischief of devils ( Devilthorn Fox ).
Some foxes of Shenmeng are sapient and appear in spirit form (e.g. Nine-Tail White Fox ). It's still unknown if any regular foxes exist on this plane.
In Setessa , foxes feed on hydras , giants , and massive serpents becoming giants ( Vulpine Goliath ). The fox is also the symbol for Bassara Tower, a watchtower near the Summer Nexus.
